# Samebase

> Samebase standardizes web apps on the best stack we have found: code in the user's GitHub
> repository, a Convex backend, and Cloudflare Workers delivery. Once you have found the best
> stack, repeat it. Each new app adds a product, not another system to maintain.

Samebase can create a new app in about a minute or connect an existing GitHub repository without
touching its providers. A connected app can remain GitHub-only or attach Convex and Cloudflare
later. In a monorepo, Samebase derives resource locations from each selected convex.json file and
each Worker's live Workers Builds root.

The Samebase starter's core local workflow runs natively on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Its
repository automation is TypeScript run directly by Node 24, so it does not require Bash or WSL.

The dashboard gives humans one inventory of every repository they connect, its provider resources,
derived locations, current state, direct provider coordinates, and provider or connection repair
actions.
Every Samebase action checks its own authentication. Authentication status is a diagnostic action,
not a preflight.
Inventory reports Samebase-owned workflow state and stable resource IDs. It coordinates explicit
Samebase actions; it is not proof of live provider state. Use provider-native tools to verify
current provider existence, configuration, deployment state, and logs unless an explicit Samebase
action exposes that live read.
Codex and Claude Code can add the public
[samebase/plugin](https://github.com/samebase/plugin) marketplace and install
`samebase@samebase`. That value means the `samebase` plugin from the `samebase` marketplace.
It is not an npm package name. The plugin packages the create or connect, local repository build,
and Git-backed hosting workflows. Cursor and other MCP clients can call the same actions directly.

Apps created through Samebase live in the user's own GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare accounts.
Deleting the Samebase account does not stop a running app. The knowledge is free: anyone can build
the identical stack with no Samebase account.

Samebase runs on the same base it gives users. The public template,
[samebase/base](https://github.com/samebase/base), is published automatically from the Samebase
monorepo as the base improves, and each template commit names the Samebase build it came from. The
template, the agent skills, and the [plugin](https://github.com/samebase/plugin) are open source
under Apache 2.0. The samebase.com control plane that creates, connects, and tracks apps is not.

The `.md` links under Docs return raw markdown, and the same paths without `.md` serve the
HTML pages. Action and operate docs are raw markdown only.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://samebase.com/): the best-stack opinion, the connected-app
  inventory, and the four claims: yours, safer, lanes, cheaper
- [The stack](https://samebase.com/docs/the-stack.md): what the app template ships and why each
  piece was chosen
- [Cloudflare setup](https://samebase.com/docs/cloudflare-setup.md): create the first Workers Builds
  API token, then let Samebase create the real Worker
- [Do it yourself](https://samebase.com/docs/do-it-yourself.md): deploy the same stack by hand, for
  $0/month, with no Samebase account
- [Receipts](https://samebase.com/docs/receipts.md): every factual claim with its primary source
  and the date it was last checked
- [Pricing](https://samebase.com/pricing.md): the Free and Pro connection limits, member limits, and
  monthly prices

## Actions

Every operational action has one contract, and these are the same actions the dashboard buttons run.
Choose an explicit action whose contract matches the required stable IDs, then reread inventory.

- [List Samebase repositories](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/get_user_repositories.md): List the Samebase repositories available to the authenticated user, including attached provider resources.
- [List Cloudflare Workers Builds tokens](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/list_workers_build_tokens.md): List the non-secret Workers Builds token names and UUIDs in the Cloudflare account connected to a Samebase organization, with its available last-used UUID.
- [Create Samebase app](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_repository.md): Create a new Samebase app. A current Workers Builds token provisions GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare; a confirmed empty token list provisions GitHub and Convex and leaves Cloudflare pending.
- [Connect existing repository](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/connect_existing_repository.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first to avoid a duplicate connection. Connect a GitHub repository by its githubRepositoryDatabaseId as a Samebase repository, then sync its repository tree. Convex and Cloudflare stay unconfigured until explicitly attached.
- [Discover Convex projects](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/discover_convex_projects.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Discover Convex code locations in the Samebase repository's GitHub repository and projects available through the connected Convex team.
- [Discover Cloudflare Workers](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/discover_cloudflare_workers.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Discover Workers in the Samebase repository's stored Cloudflare account and observe which ones are connected to its GitHub repository and live Workers Builds roots.
- [Attach Convex projects](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/attach_convex_projects.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Attach selected existing Convex projects to a Samebase repository at discovered repository code locations.
- [Attach Cloudflare Workers](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/attach_cloudflare_workers.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Attach selected existing Cloudflare Workers to a Samebase repository after re-verifying their identities and live GitHub repository roots.
- [Create Cloudflare Worker](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_cloudflare_worker.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Create and attach a Cloudflare Worker in the Samebase repository's stored Cloudflare account, configure Workers Builds for that repository root, and request the first production build.
- [Configure Workers Builds for GitHub](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/configure_workers_builds_for_github.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Configure the selected Worker's production and preview Workers Builds triggers for the Samebase repository's GitHub repository, then start a production build.
- [Rotate Convex deploy keys for Workers Builds](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/rotate_convex_deploy_keys_for_workers_builds.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Requires a verified empty Worker preview list. Rotate Samebase-named production and preview Convex deploy keys, write each value as CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY in Production and Previews Base build settings, respectively, and start a production build.
- [Retry infrastructure provisioning](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/retry_infrastructure_provisioning.md): Call repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories first and use its returned repositoryId. Retry a failed managed provisioning run for a Samebase-managed app, resuming from the failed step.
- [Submit Samebase feedback](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/submit_feedback.md): Email one feedback report to Samebase staff. After a clear Samebase product or plugin problem, draft a short report that states what the user tried, what happened, and what should improve. Show the exact report and say that you can send it automatically with no form. Call only after the user approves that exact text. A direct request to send specified feedback is approval. Call once and do not retry unless the user asks. Do not include credentials, file contents, full logs, or unrelated conversation.
- [Create browser handoff](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/create_browser_handoff.md): Create a short-lived one-time Samebase browser sign-in URL for the MCP grant's current user. The URL is sensitive and expires quickly.
- [Get authentication status](https://samebase.com/docs/actions/get_authentication_status.md): Read the caller's current Samebase MCP authentication state: account identity, role, access keys, and OAuth token scopes.

## Operate

- [Agent plugin](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/agent-plugin.md): install `samebase@samebase`
  for the building and Git-backed hosting workflows around this action catalog
- [MCP server](https://api.samebase.com/mcp): connect a coding agent over MCP (OAuth happens in the
  browser); the tools are the actions listed above.
- [Production logs](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/production-logs.md): read backend and Worker
  logs provider-direct, with coordinates from repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories
- [Custom domain](https://samebase.com/docs/operate/custom-domain.md): attach a domain to the
  app's Worker in your own Cloudflare account
